SMTO-CTX-0022 — SMTO couldn't finish cleaning up a conversation's attached files

GUID: ba7a456a-9831-446c-8410-8a938b588898
Slug: context-store-invalid
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • While removing a conversation, SMTO hit a problem in its own code when tidying up that conversation's attached files. The removal most likely did not finish, so the conversation may still be listed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at your conversation list to see whether the conversation you were deleting is still there. This tells you whether the deletion stopped before it made any changes.
  2. Open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The problem is inside SMTO's code; the error alone does not establish a repair you can safely do yourself, but the copied details show where it happened.
  3. If this appeared during automatic cleanup, note the settings shown in Settings › Data › Auto-purge and include them when you report it. Automatic cleanup uses the same step, so it will keep hitting this problem until SMTO is fixed.

What success looks like

  • After SMTO is updated, deleting the conversation removes it from the list without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details and your SMTO version to the person who installed SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder or files inside it by hand; that won't fix this and can lose other conversations.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • ContextStore.release_conversation_in was called with a database selector other than main or native_db during conversation deletion or purge; this is an internal call error, not damaged stored data.

What this means

  • The context-release helper accepts only main or native_db as its attached database selector; another selector is an internal call-contract error, not evidence of damaged stored data. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The context-release helper accepts only main or native_db as its attached database selector; another selector is an internal call-contract error, not evidence of damaged stored data.

How to diagnose it

  • Preserve the call stage and installed version for support; inspect the caller's database selector rather than editing or deleting the context store.

How to fix it

  • No direct repair is available for this occurrence. Use the supported investigation or alternative workflow below.
  • This is a code-level defect: the caller of ContextStore.release_conversation_in (conversation_management.py, retention.py or memory_retention.py) passed an unsupported schema value. Report the error ID, the stack trace from the Server log and the installed version; do not delete, rewrite or change permissions on the context database, since that cannot fix an invalid selector.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The caller uses an allowed database selector and releases only the intended conversation's grants.

What not to do

  • Do not delete, rewrite or loosen access to the context database to repair an invalid internal selector.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
